key: Two brothers in a joint family argue
name: ch14_brothers_shared_goal
alt: Two brothers stop arguing over Rishikesh or Kerala when their elder sister points to the goal they share: a restful, beautiful trip for their parents.
scene: A wide living-room view in an Indian joint-family home, warm evening light from a window on the right. LEFT: a younger brother (about 30, teal kurta) leans forward on a sofa, one finger raised, with a small thought bubble above him showing snowy mountains and a river. RIGHT: an older brother (about 35, plum shirt, spectacles) faces him with arms crossed, his own thought bubble showing a backwater houseboat and coconut palms. Between their bubbles a short zig-zag line of crossed arrows shows the ten minutes of going round in circles. CENTRE, standing slightly behind the sofa: their elder sister (about 40, coral saree, hair in a bun) with an open palm raised, calm and smiling. Above her a larger rounded bubble joins both brothers' bubbles with two dashed arrows: inside it an elderly couple sit relaxed on a bench under a tree, a small heart and a gentle sun beside them. In the lower foreground on the coffee table lie a printed train timetable and a phone with a map, which the brothers will turn to next. Mood: tension easing into agreement, both brothers starting to nod. Label: "SAME GOAL" in capitals above the sister's shared bubble at the top centre.

key: At a Sunday family lunch, your uncle
name: ch14_uncle_scooter_never
alt: At a family lunch an uncle has already declared NEVER to electric scooters, so every fact bounces off his public word; an inset shows the earlier moment when two easy yes answers came first.
scene: A split-panel picture with a thin vertical divider in the middle. LEFT panel: a Sunday family lunch around a long dining table with steel plates, rice, dal and papad. A moustached uncle in his late 50s (cream kurta, slightly bald) sits at the head of the table with his arms folded and chin up, a speech bubble above him reading "NEVER". A young nephew (mid-20s, teal T-shirt) opposite him holds out small cards with icons: a coin with a road for running cost, a ticket for the subsidy, a smiling neighbour face. The cards bounce off an invisible wall in front of the uncle, shown by curved dashed arrows rebounding, and two other relatives at the table watch, making the uncle's word public. RIGHT panel: the same two people earlier, standing at a petrol pump, the uncle looking ruefully at a meter that spins high; the nephew asks a question, and the uncle answers with two small green speech bubbles each holding a tick, one after the other, while a plain scooter waits at the edge with no logo. Mood: left stubborn and stuck, right easy and friendly. Labels: "NO FIRST" above the left panel and "YES FIRST" above the right panel.

key: A clerk at a post office savings counter
name: ch14_post_office_nominee
alt: A post office clerk helps an elderly man see that naming his daughter as nominee gets her the money in a week instead of months of court papers.
scene: Inside an Indian post office savings counter seen from the customer side: a wooden counter, a steel grille window, a wall clock and a calendar behind the clerk. RIGHT, behind the grille: a friendly woman clerk in her 40s (amber saree, spectacles, pen in hand) leans forward, smiling, pointing with her pen at a form on the counter. LEFT, in front of the counter: an elderly man in his 70s (white kurta, grey sleeveless jacket, white hair, walking stick) who has just stopped waving the form away; now he looks thoughtful, one hand on his chin. The form on the counter is large and clear, with one empty column highlighted and labelled. Above the two of them float two thought bubbles from the man: one shows a young woman (his daughter) receiving an envelope next to a small calendar showing one week with a green tick; the other shows a tall stack of court papers and a long hourglass with a red cross. A dashed arrow runs from the highlighted column to the happy bubble. A small extra passbook for a grandson lies near his hand. Soft morning light, calm and kind mood. Labels: "NOMINEE" on the highlighted form column, "1 WEEK" beside the small calendar in the happy bubble.

key: A customer at a pressure-cooker shop
name: ch14_cooker_handle_lid
alt: A shop owner agrees with an angry customer, then through simple questions she realises the handle stays cool and only the lid gets hot.
scene: Inside a small kitchenware shop in Chennai with steel shelves full of pressure cookers and vessels in the background. LEFT: a woman customer in her 30s (plum saree, handbag on her shoulder) holds up a new steel pressure cooker by its black handle, her face moving from annoyance to realisation; a small "!" badge near her earlier frown. RIGHT, behind a wooden counter: the shop owner in his 50s (white half-sleeve shirt, veshti, moustache) nods with an open hand, agreeing, not arguing. CENTRE, as a large clear inset, the cooker is shown up close: the black handle with a green tick and a blue cool wavy line, and the steel lid with the whistle giving off steam lines and a red heat glow. Thin arrows point from the labels to each part. On the counter lie a folded cotton cloth and a small packet with a rubber gasket ring, the second gasket she buys on her way out. Two small speech bubbles with ticks above the customer show her saying yes twice. Bright daylight from the shop front, mood turning friendly. Labels: "COOL" pointing to the handle, "HOT" pointing to the lid.

key: You call a tent-house in Jaipur
name: ch14_tent_house_package
alt: One tent-house refuses a small order of 50 chairs; another asks three questions and offers a home package of chairs, a shamiana and two fans.
scene: A split-panel picture with a thin vertical divider. LEFT panel: a man in his 40s (teal shirt) at home holds a phone to his ear with a puzzled face; a phone bubble from the first tent-house shows a stack of many chairs with a red cross and the line going dead, a broken dashed line and a small phone with a cross. RIGHT panel: a sunny courtyard of a Jaipur home with a pink-ochre wall and an arched doorway. A colourful striped shamiana canopy is set up, under it neat rows of plastic chairs (draw about twelve to imply fifty) and two pedestal fans on either side. A tent-house owner in his 50s (amber turban, white kurta) stands beside it, and three small speech bubbles above him each hold a green tick for the three yes answers: home function, forty or fifty people, a package for the same price. The same customer from the left panel shakes his hand, smiling. A small wedding garland and calendar on the wall hint that he will book them again. Bright afternoon light. Labels: "MIN 200" in the left phone bubble, "PACKAGE" above the shamiana on the right.

key: A good maths teacher at a Kota coaching
name: ch14_kota_teacher_questions
alt: A coaching-class maths teacher asks small questions until the student spots his own mistake, 26 instead of 36.
scene: A coaching-centre classroom in Kota with a big whiteboard, a ceiling fan and rows of benches. On the whiteboard LEFT: a large square drawn in marker with one side marked and a small area formula beside it. CENTRE: a young woman teacher in her 30s (teal salwar kameez, dupatta, marker in hand) stands beside the board, not frowning, just asking, with three small question bubbles stacked above her, each with a question mark. RIGHT, in the front bench: a teenage boy of 16 (white school-style shirt, backpack beside him) looks down at his open notebook, eyes wide with the moment of discovery, a small light bulb above him. The notebook is shown in a large inset: the written answer crossed out by his own pen and the correct answer written next to it, with his pencil still in his hand. A curved dashed arrow runs from the board square to the notebook, showing that the student follows the chain himself. Two other students sit in the background, blurred and smaller. Mood: calm, proud, no embarrassment. Labels: "SIDE 6" along the square on the board, "26" crossed out and "36" written beside it in the notebook inset.
